standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic minor maintenance checks task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner chooses four or five real check points in the household that commonly need periodic attention, writes what a normal condition versus a needs-attention condition looks like for each one, physically checks each point, and reports the findings to the household so an adult can decide what happens next.
safetyNotes: Checking whether a smoke detector's test button works, a filter looks clean, or a faucet drips is different from repairing any of them; any actual repair, part replacement, or fix beyond a simple check is for the adults in your household, not the learner.

simulationAlternative.description: If the learner cannot safely or physically access certain areas of the household, the learner instead reviews a provided written description of five common minor-maintenance items, decides for each one whether the described condition is normal, needs attention, or needs a trusted adult right away, and drafts the report they would give the household based on those descriptions.

materials: learner-local: a flashlight, if needed to see a check point clearly
adult-or-local: access to the household areas being checked

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Describe how you reported your findings to the household, what the household's response was, and name the one check point you think most needs a trusted adult's attention soon.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Checklist accuracy and specificity: At least four check points are listed with a normal and a needs-attention description written before the walkthrough. | Boundary-respecting report: No repair is attempted, and findings are reported to the household with at least one item flagged for adult attention if needed. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add two more check points to their list, look into what a trusted household resource, such as an appliance manual or manufacturer's guidance, says about how often each item should be checked, and note that schedule next to each item.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: minor maintenance checks worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner chooses four or five real check points in the household that commonly need periodic attention, writes what a normal condition versus a needs-attention condition looks like for each one, physically checks each point, and reports the findings to the household so an adult can decide what happens next.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact minor maintenance checks decision or action.
Model move 2: Pick four or five real check points in the household that commonly need periodic attention.
Model move 3: For each check point, write what a normal condition looks like and what a needs-attention condition looks like, so you know what you are checking for before you start.

Model check: Checklist accuracy and specificity: At least four check points are listed with a normal and a needs-attention description written before the walkthrough. | Boundary-respecting report: No repair is attempted, and findings are reported to the household with at least one item flagged for adult attention if needed.

resources.title: minor maintenance checks action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for minor maintenance checks.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: minor maintenance checks coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner chooses four or five real check points in the household that commonly need periodic attention, writes what a normal condition versus a needs-attention condition looks like for each one, physically checks each point, and reports the findings to the household so an adult can decide what happens next.
Coach direction: Pick four or five real check points in the household that commonly need periodic attention.
Learner prompt: List the check points you picked and name one of them you have never actually looked at closely before.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: minor maintenance checks complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each check point, write what a normal condition looks like and what a needs-attention condition looks like, so you know what you are checking for before you start.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I wrote a normal-condition description and a needs-attention description for at least four check points.
Response 2 (t2-p2): At least one of my check points involves testing something, like pressing a smoke detector's test button, rather than only looking at it.

Equal-access rule: If the learner cannot safely or physically access certain areas of the household, the learner instead reviews a provided written description of five common minor-maintenance items, decides for each one whether the described condition is normal, needs attention, or needs a trusted adult right away, and drafts the report they would give the household based on those descriptions.

resources.title: minor maintenance checks minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe how you reported your findings to the household, what the household's response was, and name the one check point you think most needs a trusted adult's attention soon.

Success checks: Checklist accuracy and specificity: At least four check points are listed with a normal and a needs-attention description written before the walkthrough. | Boundary-respecting report: No repair is attempted, and findings are reported to the household with at least one item flagged for adult attention if needed.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: minor maintenance checks supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional minor maintenance checks condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Checklist accuracy and specificity: At least four check points are listed with a normal and a needs-attention description written before the walkthrough. | Boundary-respecting report: No repair is attempted, and findings are reported to the household with at least one item flagged for adult attention if needed..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: minor maintenance checks — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
For each check point, write what a normal condition looks like and what a needs-attention condition looks like, so you know what you are checking for before you start.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: minor maintenance checks — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Checklist accuracy and specificity: At least four check points are listed with a normal and a needs-attention description written before the walkthrough. | Boundary-respecting report: No repair is attempted, and findings are reported to the household with at least one item flagged for adult attention if needed.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
